title: Measured geometry and horizon dynamics of the SU(2) gauge orbit space: scale-free curvature, a localization-coherence crossover, and a coherence-gated horizon-gluon correlation
description: Numerical measurements, to our knowledge the first, of orbit-space curvature observables on sampled SU(2) lattice ensembles, and of the dynamics of the approach to the Gribov horizon. Includes: scale-free curvature bounds addressing Singer's curvature route with a mechanism; two Haar-disorder constants; a coupling-driven localization-coherence crossover of the lowest Faddeev-Popov mode (controlled at fixed physical volume); and a coherence-gated per-configuration correlation between horizon proximity and infrared gluon power, verified by a pre-registered out-of-sample prediction (run 10) and a twelve-ensemble blind scan fitting the frozen zero-parameter activation curve at chi2/dof = 1.00 (run 11); one pre-registered independence control failed honestly, so the claim is stated as a gated correlation, not a law. Contains the manuscript, all validated instruments and GPU notebooks (reproducible on free Kaggle GPUs), raw results, the append-only research ledger (every claim's falsifier fixed before its data; 13 refuted conjectures documented), and interactive visualizations. Research by Nitin Pandey in close collaboration with Claude (Anthropic). No claim herein bears on the existence of the Yang-Mills mass gap at infinite volume.
